target: Security keys are rotated at renewal times with independent identically distributed intervals X. Historical intervals have E[X]=10 days and E[X^2]=200 days^2. An auditor arrives at a uniformly random stationary time, not at a rotation epoch, and needs the expected time until the next rotation. The variability of rotation intervals must be accounted for; simply taking half the mean interval is not accepted.
surface: A previous security audit assumed arrival uniformly within a typical 10-day interval and forecast half of 10, or 5 days, until the next key rotation.
structural: A passenger arriving at a random stationary time to a renewal bus service encountered the inspection paradox. The equilibrium mean residual waiting time was E[X^2]/(2E[X]), because longer intervals are sampled more often; it equals half the mean only for deterministic equal intervals.
rubric: Explicitly selects the stationary renewal residual-life/inspection-paradox formula.
Reports expected time 10 days rather than the naive 5.
States iid stationary renewal/random-time arrival and finite-second-moment assumptions.
